data.title: We're Not Very Worried About Unigold's (CVE:UGD) Cash Burn Rate
data.description:
Even when a business is losing money, it's possible for shareholders to make money if they buy a good business at the right price. For example, although software-as-a-service business Salesforce.com lost money for years while it grew recurring revenue, if you held shares since 2005, you'd have done very well indeed. But while the successes are well known, investors should not ignore the very many unprofitable companies that simply burn through all their cash and collapse.

So, the natural question for Unigold (CVE:UGD) shareholders is whether they should be concerned by its rate of cash burn. For the purpose of this article, we'll define cash burn as the amount of cash the company is spending each year to fund its growth (also called its negative free cash flow). The first step is to compare its cash burn with its cash reserves, to give us its 'cash runway'.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Does Unigold Have A Long Cash Runway?

You can calculate a company's cash runway by dividing the amount of cash it has by the rate at which it is spending that cash. In June 2026, Unigold had CA$10m in cash, and was debt-free. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through CA$2.2m. So it had a cash runway of about 4.6 years from June 2026. There's no doubt that this is a reassuringly long runway. The image below shows how its cash balance has been changing over the last few years.

View our latest analysis for Unigold

How Is Unigold's Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

Unigold didn't record any revenue over the last year, indicating that it's an early stage company still developing its business. Nonetheless, we can still examine its cash burn trajectory as part of our assessment of its cash burn situation. Over the last year its cash burn actually increased by 38%, which suggests that management are increasing investment in future growth, but not too quickly. However, the company's true cash runway will therefore be shorter than suggested above, if spending continues to increase. Unigold makes us a little nervous due to its lack of substantial operating revenue. We prefer most of the stocks on this list of stocks that analysts expect to grow.

Can Unigold Raise More Cash Easily?

Given its cash burn trajectory, Unigold shareholders may wish to consider how easily it could raise more cash, despite its solid cash runway. Companies can raise capital through either debt or equity. Commonly, a business will sell new shares in itself to raise cash and drive growth. We can compare a company's cash burn to its market capitalisation to get a sense for how many new shares a company would have to issue to fund one year's operations.

Unigold has a market capitalisation of CA$61m and burnt through CA$2.2m last year, which is 3.5% of the company's market value. That's a low proportion, so we figure the company would be able to raise more cash to fund growth, with a little dilution, or even to simply borrow some money.

So, Should We Worry About Unigold's Cash Burn?

It may already be apparent to you that we're relatively comfortable with the way Unigold is burning through its cash. In particular, we think its cash runway stands out as evidence that the company is well on top of its spending. While its increasing cash burn wasn't great, the other factors mentioned in this article more than make up for weakness on that measure. Looking at all the measures in this article, together, we're not worried about its rate of cash burn; the company seems well on top of its medium-term spending needs. On another note, we conducted an in-depth investigation of the company, and identified 3 warning signs for Unigold (1 doesn't sit too well with us!) that you should be aware of before investing here.

data.title: 3 European Gas Stocks Retail Investors Are Watching As Winter Supply Risks Return
data.description:
European gas markets are back in the spotlight as a rare mix of early polar vortex disruption, El Niño and thin storage cushions raises fresh questions about how secure winter energy really looks. Sudden swings in demand, tighter LNG supply and jumpy prices can reshape cash flows across the sector fast, which creates both openings and risks. This article looks at 3 European natural gas and LNG infrastructure stocks exposed to these weather and supply shocks and explains how the current setup could matter for long term investors.

The three stocks below are just a starting sample from this European gas and LNG theme, and the full screen surfaced 13 more sizeable companies with equally compelling narratives that are not covered here. Yü Group (AIM:YU.)

Overview: Yü Group supplies electricity, gas and water to UK businesses, coupling energy retail with metering assets and related engineering services.

Operations: The group generates approximately £765 million of revenue in the United Kingdom, tying its fortunes closely to domestic energy conditions.

Market Cap: £309 million

Yü Group sits close to the fault line of UK gas and power pricing. According to European_Hidden_Gem_Stocks, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the way management is reshaping the business model matters directly for how this exposure plays out over the next few years.

"Management is targeting a significant increase in market share, while expanding cross-selling opportunities across electricity, gas, water and engineering services. At the same time, the company is building a growing portfolio of owned smart meters that generate recurring rental income while creating valuable customer data."

What happens to future profitability depends heavily on how one unseen pressure on unit economics ultimately feeds through to that evolving model.

That hidden pressure point is exactly what the full narrative for Yü Group unpacks, including how meter assets and cross selling could accelerate or stall the whole plan.

Fortum Oyj (HLSE:FORTUM)

Overview: Fortum Oyj is a Nordic utility that produces and sells electricity and heat, runs power and gas retail services, and supports decarbonization for households, businesses and industrial clients across several European markets.

Operations: Fortum generates most of its €7.7b revenue from Generation at €3.5b and Consumer Solutions at €3.7b, with earnings concentrated in the Nordics.

Market Cap: €20.1b

Fortum Oyj offers European gas and LNG investors a different angle on the theme, with low carbon Nordic generation and heat assets whose earnings sensitivity still links back to regional gas pricing, which is exactly what the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St focuses on in its current view.

"The 22 year nuclear power purchase agreement with Google that covers half of Loviisa’s capacity from 2030 to 2049 and is expected to lift group return on net assets by about 1.4 percentage points provides a long dated earnings stream that helps justify current valuation levels."

What happens to future returns hinges on how one unresolved pressure in Fortum Oyj’s retail and flexibility economics ultimately shapes group margins.

That margin question is exactly what the full narrative for Fortum Oyj tackles. It reveals how retail economics, nuclear contracts and gas exposure could be accelerating a quieter reset in Fortum Oyj’s earnings mix.

Drax Group (LSE:DRX)

Overview: Drax Group runs UK biomass and renewable power stations that provide dispatchable electricity and grid support, with revenues influenced by gas-linked power prices.

Operations: Drax Group generates most of its £7.6b revenue from Biomass Generation at £4.1b and Energy Solutions at £2.4b, with smaller contributions from Pellet Production and Flexible Generation.

Market Cap: £2.77b

Drax Group fits this gas and LNG screen as a renewable-heavy generator whose earnings still ebb and flow with UK gas-driven power pricing. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St frames the appeal around how contracted low carbon output and flexible capacity might interact with that volatility.

"The recent agreement on a government backed low carbon dispatchable CfD for Drax Power Station, covering all units through 2031, continues to anchor long term revenue visibility and limit merchant power price exposure, which can support more predictable EBITDA and cash flow profiles than the share price appears to reflect."

What happens to future margins and cash generation hinges on how pressure in funding and executing the UK build out ultimately plays through.

That funding question is only the start, and the full narrative for Drax Group shows how Drax Group’s contracted base could be masking both upside optionality and real execution risk.

According to J_Tyrader, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the key near term swing factor is how upcoming results either confirm or challenge the quality of recent earnings, especially with large one off items in the mix.

High reliance on external borrowing and the need to prove earnings quality remain central.
